analysis.title: One Test Too Many: BTIG's Krinsky Targets 7,000 With SPX "Livin' On A Prayer"
key_insights: BTIG's Krinsky sees risk of the S&P 500 falling to the 7,000-7,100 zone, after a high of 7,844 in early October and a level near 7,320 on Nov 18. He expects a break below the 200-day moving average.
The S&P is testing the 7,250-7,350 support zone for the fifth time since early June. Krinsky argues repeated tests of one level raise the odds that it breaks.

The S&P fell below its 200-day moving average on the morning of Nov 18, from 7,388 at 10:24am to about 7,320 by 11:04am. Krinsky says small caps, mid caps, the Nasdaq, semis, industrials and transports were already below their 200-day averages.
A move to 7,000 would put the S&P about 10.8% below its October high, which is correction territory. The top of the 7,000-7,100 zone is about 9.5% below the peak.
Last Thursday Krinsky called the bounce above 7,600 a gift to sell and expected a stall below the downtrend line near 7,700. The S&P went from roughly 7,632 to about 7,320 in three sessions.

The Russell 2000 (IWM) closed at $271.51, about 2.9% below its 200-day average, on its third test of support since October. Krinsky says it does not look like a bottom after weeks of churning around that average.
Mid caps (MDY) sit about 1.2% below their 200-day average and above the May lows near $650. Krinsky sees the same story and no bottom.
The Nasdaq Composite was at 24,407, nearly 3% below its 200-day average, on its third test of the July lows. Krinsky says the support held in July and last week.
The iShares software ETF (IGV) fell 3.4% on the day to $95.60. It lost the 100 line it reclaimed in August and its rising trendline off the April lows, and sits about 1.4% above its 200-day average.

Krinsky repeats his Sunday call that Apple (Not Rated) is likely to trade materially lower over the coming weeks, after it hit 52-week highs on back-to-back days and closed more than 1% below each. Historically 20-day returns after that signal were negative 89% of the time.
Krinsky rejects the argument that the market is oversold. He says oversold conditions were used up around Nov 5 and the market is now in a weaker spot.
Morgan Stanley went max overweight stocks with an 8,700 S&P target for 2027 and a 6,000 bear case. The article cites it as the counterpoint to Krinsky's 7,000 view.

market_movers.rationale: BTIG (Not Rated) says the 52-week-high exhaustion signal shows a high likelihood AAPL trades materially lower in the coming weeks. The article's math puts a 12.57% average drop near $307, close to the 200-day average.

sector_views.rationale: IGV lost its August reclaim of the 100 line and its rising trendline off the April lows, and now sits near its 200-day average.
IWM is below its 200-day average on a third test of support and MDY is about 1.2% below its average. Krinsky says neither looks like a bottom.
Krinsky calls Apple still a cyclical tech company, and the Nasdaq and semis are already below their 200-day averages.

earnings_insights: Nvidia's first earnings report without Jensen Huang is days away, listed among the risks facing the S&P (upcoming, no estimate given).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Krinsky's minimum downside zone after a break of the 200-day average. A 7,000 print would be a 10.8% correction from the October high.
Morgan Stanley's bull target sits against a bear case 1,000 points below Krinsky's 7,000, which the article reads as a wide range of outcomes.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The article lists a possible 50bps move as one of the pressures on the index.

risk_factors: The 2-year yield is pricing a Fed openly debating a 50bps move on Dec 9.
Nvidia reports its first earnings without Jensen Huang within days.
The article lists a growing number of critical-system outages, including Microsoft 365, the FAA, banks and the NSA's classified network.
Failed bounces have burned off oversold readings without repairing the charts.
charts_described: BTIG chart shows two dashed lines for the S&P: the 7,350 shelf it has leaned on since June and the 7,000 line below where the index topped out last winter before the April breakout.
BTIG chart of IGV shows it lost the 100 line reclaimed in August and the rising trendline off the April lows.
vol_and_positioning: Goldman's futures desk saw Russell 2000 funding richen by 13bps on Nov 11, more than twice the typical daily move. The article reads it as retail levering up in small caps ahead of the front-end selloff while institutions went the other way.
On Nov 5 the semis index fell 12% and every S&P sector closed red. Krinsky called it early signs of capitulation but far from a full washout.
AAPL hit 52-week highs on back-to-back days and closed more than 1% below the high on each, which Krinsky calls a sign of upside exhaustion.
cross_bank_references: Morgan Stanley went max overweight stocks with an 8,700 S&P target for 2027, against BTIG's 7,000 downside target.
Goldman's futures desk spotted Russell 2000 funding richen by 13bps on Nov 11.

tension_points.bull_case: Morgan Stanley went max overweight stocks with an 8,700 S&P target for 2027, reasoning that with risk assets having cheapened it embraces risk. The article also allows that the fifth test of support could hold like the first four.
tension_points.bear_case: BTIG's Krinsky sees a break below the 200-day average toward 7,000-7,100 after five tests of 7,250-7,350. The other indices are already below their 200-day averages and the oversold conditions of Nov 5 have been used up.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hold of the 7,250-7,350 support zone on the fifth test, which the article concedes is possible.
